newsitem.title: UK: BP seeks order to block Greenpeace Foinaven action.
newsitem.headline: BP seeks order to block Greenpeace Foinaven action.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc said on Monday it had requested a court injunction to prevent Greenpeace from further hindering its oil exploration activity in the north Atlantic.
"BP has requested the courts for an injunction restraining Greenpeace from hindering or interfering with our legal activities west of Shetland," a BP spokesman said.
The request follows a protest by the environmental campaign group last week which delayed the Stena Dee drilling rig, on charter to BP to develop its offshore Foinaven project.
The Greenpeace campaigners clambered aboard the floating platform which was heading from Norway to the Foinaven field some 100 miles off the coast of Scotland.

On Monday BP said it was suing Greenpeace for 1.4 million pounds ($2.3 million) to try to reclaim the costs incurred in halting progress of the rig which is on hire at a cost of more than 100,000 pounds per day.
Greenpeace said BP had issued the claim in Scotland's highest civil court, the Court of Session, against it and four individuals who took part in the protest.
Greenpeace said a hearing where BP will call for an interim ruling against the group was due to be held on Tuesday.
The law suit threatens to bankrupt the campaign group. Greenpeace said assets had already been frozen, pending the interim hearing.
BP said it was not seeking to put Greenpeace out of business but wanted to recoup some of the costs resulting from delays to Stena Dee.
"We are not trying to stop Greenpeace protesting but we do object to being physically impeded and to the costs incurred," said the BP spokesman.
Greenpeace called off its Stena Dee occupation on Sunday, saying it could no longer guarantee the safety of the protestors.
The four were each fined 200 pounds in a Scottish court on Monday for their part in the action.
The group has applied for a judicial review opposing further exploration in the region.
Greenpeace had also been blocking an Atlantic Richfield Co rig off the Alaskan coast to keep it away from a field in the Arctic Beaufort Sea.
A U.S. federal judge ordered the activists on Friday to stay outside a moving safety buffer around the mobile rig.
The blockades, aimed at fighting global warming, are part of Greenpeace's most ambitious campaign yet against the oil industry.
The group wants oil producers to switch to renewable resources, arguing that burning existing reserves of fossil fuels will cause irreversible climate change.
